seoTitle: Set Existing Contacts as Marketing Contacts in HubSpot
metaDescription: Learn how to reclassify existing HubSpot contacts as marketing contacts using bulk edit, and how to keep an eye on your monthly subscription limits.
intro: HubSpot bills separately for non-marketing records and marketing-eligible contacts, so if you want to email a group that's already sitting in your CRM, you need to flip their status manually first. This guide walks through the actual navigation — from the home dashboard into CRM, then into the Contacts table — filtering to the right segment, selecting records, and running the bulk update that marks them as marketing contacts. It also covers why that confirmation step and the billing usage meter matter before you commit a large batch.

steps.heading: Start from your HubSpot home dashboard
steps.body: Logging into HubSpot lands you on a home screen greeting you by name, with today's meetings, an empty task list, and an activity feed prompting you to connect your calendar and inbox. The left-hand navigation here is the spine of the whole app — Home, CRM, Marketing, Content, Sales, Commerce, Service, Data Management, Automation, and Reporting all live in this same rail. Contacts isn't visible yet at this level; it's tucked one layer down inside CRM, which is worth knowing since it's easy to go hunting for it under Sales instead.

image.caption: The HubSpot home dashboard, with the left navigation rail collapsed to its top-level sections before CRM is expanded.

steps.heading: Open CRM and go to Contacts
steps.body: Hovering the CRM item in the left rail expands a flyout with Contacts, Companies, Deals, Tickets, and Orders at the top, followed by Segments (Lists), Inbox, Calls, Meetings, Tasks, Playbooks, Message Templates, and Snippets further down. Contacts is the first item in that list and takes you to your full database in table form. If you only need a specific subset of contacts, Segments (Lists) right below it is where any saved views you've already built will be waiting.

image.caption: The CRM flyout menu from the home dashboard, with Contacts as the first option above Companies, Deals, and Segments (Lists).

steps.heading: Filter to the segment you want to update
steps.body: On the Contacts screen, a row of tabs across the top separates saved views like All contacts, Newsletter subscribers, Unsubscribed, and All customers, and the table itself gives you filters for Contact owner, Create date, Last activity date, and Lead status, plus an Advanced filters option for anything more specific. If you're reclassifying a group tied to a past import or campaign, building a filter here first keeps you from scrolling through unrelated records. A small sample table might show just a couple of rows, like two test contacts with placeholder emails, but the same filtering and selection mechanics apply whether you're working with two records or two thousand.

image.caption: The Contacts table with its All contacts tab active, showing the checkbox column, search bar, and Filters, Sort, and Advanced filters controls.

steps.heading: Select the target rows
steps.body: Once your view is filtered to the right group, check the box in the table header to select every visible row at once, or check individual rows if you only want a handful. HubSpot shows a running count of how many contacts are selected, which is your last chance to sanity-check the batch size before you commit — a filter that's too loose can accidentally sweep in far more contacts than you meant to reclassify.

steps.heading: Run the bulk action and confirm
steps.body: With rows selected, a refreshed toolbar appears above the table with a More dropdown; choosing Set as marketing contacts from that menu opens an inline modal explaining the change. Because this action directly affects your billing tier, HubSpot asks you to type a confirmation keyword into a safety field before the update button becomes active — a deliberate friction point so a bulk edit doesn't silently reclassify thousands of records and bump you into a higher pricing tier by accident. Clicking the update button flips the eligibility flag for every selected contact immediately.

steps.heading: Check your billing limits afterward
steps.body: After a bulk update, it's worth a quick trip to your Account & Billing settings to see the usage meter for total live marketing contacts against your plan's limit. Marketing-eligible contacts are what HubSpot actually bills against, so a large reclassification can push you close to a tier boundary even if your total database size hasn't changed. Checking this right after the update, rather than waiting for a surprise invoice, is the cheapest way to catch it.

faq.question: Does setting a contact as marketing-eligible cost extra?
faq.answer: It can. Marketing contacts count against your subscription tier, so it's worth checking your Account & Billing usage meter before and after a large bulk update.

faq.question: Can I undo marking contacts as marketing contacts?
faq.answer: Yes, you can typically switch them back to non-marketing status the same way, through the More bulk action dropdown in Contacts.

faq.question: Why do I need to type a confirmation keyword?
faq.answer: It's a safety step in the Set as marketing contacts modal to prevent accidentally reclassifying a large batch of contacts and affecting your billing tier.

faq.question: Where do I check how many marketing contacts I'm using?
faq.answer: Your Account & Billing settings show a usage meter for total live marketing contacts against your plan's limit — worth checking right after any bulk change.

faq.question: Where do I find Contacts in the HubSpot navigation?
faq.answer: From the home dashboard, hover CRM in the left rail — Contacts is the first item in the flyout menu, above Companies, Deals, and Segments (Lists).
